goal: Stops peers that disable tx relay from bypassing inbound tx-relay capacity limits via BIP35 mempool requests
Closes a resource-accounting gap that exposes bloom-filter-enabled nodes to a DoS-style bypass
reviewability: Ready to review now, CI passes and no rebase needed
Author already reworked the approach based on feedback so current code reflects resolved concerns
agreement: Protocol-change concern about flooding fRelay=false peers was resolved with a characterization test (darosior)
Design question about whether fRelay=false peers should request inventory at all led to a rework aligned with bitcoinj behavior, no further objection (gmaxwell)
No explicit ACK/NACK language used, positive read comes from concerns being resolved rather than open pushback

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it closes a genuine resource-accounting bypass around inbound tx-relay capacity limits
Affects node operators running bloom-filter-enabled nodes exposed to a peer requesting full mempool snapshots outside relay limits
Not a catastrophic or actively exploited vulnerability, so it sits below P1, but reviewer engagement confirms the mechanism matters
